messages:
anya: heads up — noticed a consistent quality dip when we drop sable-7b into llm.int8 weight-only (bitsandbytes) on the summarization eval slice. rouge-L ~ -1.8 vs fp16 on the nightly run :eyes:
matt: ouch, that's pretty big for a weight-only drop. is this the default llm.int8 config or a custom profile?
anya: default bnb.int8 + our standard deployment profile (batching=auto, kv-cache enabled). no per-layer overrides.
raj: do we have a comparison to gptq/awq for the same model? how much better/worse?
anya: quick numbers from the same harness: fp16 baseline; gptq (8/16) ~ -0.3, AWQ ~ -0.7, llm.int8 weight-only (bnb) ~ -1.8. throughput is better for bnb int8 (~1.6x vs fp16) but quality loss seems larger on longform summarize prompts.
sasha: can you paste the eval slice config and example prompt? maybe tokenizer truncation or kv-cache interplay?
anya: sure — slice is 250–2k token summaries, mix of news + docs. example prompt: ```
Summarize the following document in 5 bullet points:
<document text>
```
lucas: two quick hypotheses: 1) activation outliers causing quantization mismatch for some layers, 2) bnb per-channel scales not tuned for this model architecture. we saw similar in a different repo where folding biases helped.
matt: any chance of activating the calibration pass (per-layer minmax est) or running a short QAT-ish pass? bnb has an option to force fp32 for certain problematic layers.
anya: there's a config we tested quickly: ```
LLM_INT8_CONFIG={
  "force_fp32_layers": ["lm_head", "attn_out"],
  "quant_type": "nf4",
  "threshold": 0.02
}
```
with that rouge-L improved to -1.1 but throughput dropped to ~1.4x.
meredith: can we do a micro-bakeoff: run 3 variants (bnb-default, bnb-force-fp32-sparse, gptq-lite) across the 1000-sample summarize slice and report token-level logprob delta + hallucination rate? set canary to 3% first.
ci-bot: rollout plan created: sable-int8-bakeoff -> canary 3% -> monitor eval-hook (rouge-l, tok-logprob-delta) -> escalate to 25% if pass. (pipeline #4621) :robot_face:
raj: I'll queue the bakeoff jobs tonight. will also add an eval that records top-5 token probs so we can see distribution shifts.
sasha: also add a short-format QA slice (customer-facing API examples). we care more about concision errors there.
anya: thanks — action items: raj run bakeoff + collect per-layer activation histograms; lucas try force-fp32 candidate and a reduced-threshold nf4; meredith set canary + alert thresholds. post results here with the numbers (rouge-L, throughput p99, token-delta).
matt: if we still see >1.0 rouge drop after tuning, prefer gptq fallback variant in production (configurable at routing layer).
anya: agreed. tagging @eng-runtime to make sure fallback routing is ready for sable variants. :thumbsup:
meredith: noted — I'll add a runbook entry for sable-7b int8 fallback and document the eval slices + thresholds.
anya: great — thanks everyone. will paste first bakeoff summary here when jobs finish. :pray:
